newsitem.title: HONG KONG: World stock exchanges see no near-term Net threat.
newsitem.headline: World stock exchanges see no near-term Net threat.

text.p: World stock exchanges do not currently view trading systems on the Internet as a near-term threat to existing exchanges, Bengt Ryden, president of the International Federation of Stock Exchanges (FIBV), said.

"It will still take quite some years before the Internet will be a threat," Ryden, also president and chief executive officer of the Stockholm Stock Exchange, told reporters following the FIBV's two-day General Assembly in Hong Kong. He said established stock exchanges had the confidence of the general public.
"It is a combination of efficiency and confidence, trust...and that is something which will be very difficult for electronic trading systems," Ryden said.
The FIBV has 51 full members, representing more than 97 percent of world stock exchange market capitalisation.
